detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
detail.summary: Synthesis of how scrambling and decoherence interact to generate classical records. Chaotic unitary dynamics distribute quantum information, effectively creating 'branches' of the wavefunction. These branches are distinguished by microscopic records in the permutation sector of the system-environment state. Crucially, the transition from 'scrambled information' to 'accessible records' is not a universal process but observer-dependent. Effective redundancy arises when an observer has an accessible channel, not just when the environment holds the information.
detail.reason: Completing the required synthesis for proj-scrambling-records-01 after project handoff.

detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
detail.summary: The research synthesizes two seemingly distinct information dynamics: unitary scrambling, which distributes information globally across a system's degrees of freedom, and the formation of objective records, which relies on the local redundancy of pointer states in the environment. While scrambling can obscure system information, redundant record formation (Quantum Darwinism) creates an 'objective' perspective accessible to independent observers through decoherence. We find that redundant record formation is sensitive to interaction geometry and environmental noise, such that non-ideal interactions can, in specific regimes, enhance the broadcast of pointer information.
detail.reason: Synthesizing theoretical foundations of scrambling and record formation as requested by project focus.
